entries.title: From a research agenda to a product musicians can use
entries.summary: Music Kitchen takes shape as a personal arranging studio. The key question becomes how a musician directs the second and third revision through sound, examples, and gestures.
entries.stage: Playable browser interaction prototype. Product direction and research documented; no trained music model or user study yet.
entries.focus: Select a musical phrase, draw its contour, tap a rhythm, and hear a scoped, reversible change.
entries.next_step: Try the studio with pianist-songwriters, compare correction tasks with existing tools, then investigate humming and reference transfer.

entries.title: From survey to first experiment: what AI cannot learn from David Foster
entries.summary: The survey lands, the site goes live, and the build plan becomes a research question: can a composer's style be steered as separable layers? Imitation becomes the diagnostic, not the goal.
entries.stage: Survey published; positioning written; reward module tested. Architecture decision (autoregressive vs diffusion) open, pending the representation choice. No model trained yet.
entries.focus: Pin the composer's notes as a hard constraint; measure where imitation of Foster fails; let those failures define what annotations must carry.
entries.next_step: Build the data harness and relative-attention equivalence test; start Nord captures; choose event tokens or piano roll with real data in hand.

entries.title: ACE moves from idea to runnable experiment
entries.summary: An ACE-Step 1.5 fine-tuning pipeline now passes a synthetic end-to-end CPU smoke. Real ACE weights, the RTX PRO 5000 run, and original piano data are next.
entries.stage: ACE audio-personalization code and synthetic CPU smoke complete; no real ACE checkpoint or GPU training run yet.
entries.focus: Prepare original piano recordings and test whether ACE can learn expressive musical qualities while leaving the musician in control.
entries.next_step: Run a real-ACE GPU smoke, record and annotate original piano takes, then begin a held-out SFT pilot with rights-cleared material.

entries.title: From data to a labelled dataset: the David Foster corpus
entries.summary: The ACE experiment gets its corpus: 28 David Foster songs from two albums and a YouTube compilation, cut as whole songs, with captions drafted from the audio and confirmed by ear in a private web workbench.
entries.stage: Corpus assembled and auto-drafted; captions being confirmed; instrumental subset of 14 songs is the training set. No ACE checkpoint loaded, no GPU run yet.
entries.focus: Which of Foster's expressive qualities can ACE learn from whole instrumental songs, and which still need the musician's hand.
entries.next_step: Confirm captions and freeze the split, install the pinned ACE checkout, run the real-ACE GPU smoke, train the first SFT adapter, and listen blind against the base model.

entries.title: Music to score, score to music: the anatomy of a song generator
entries.summary: Three Suno uploads of one piano recording came back as audio and nothing readable. A technical report dissects why — codec-token language models through four lenses — and specifies the inverse: a notation-native latent that transcribes in and renders out, with latent actions as the edit primitive.
entries.stage: Technical report written and verified against primary sources (91 cited, 49 lookups). Notation-native latent specified, not trained; CLaMP 3 decoder baseline and notation round-trip test are the first experiments. No model trained yet.
entries.focus: Make the score the shared representation between audio and generation; treat a composer's annotations as the names of learned edit actions.
entries.next_step: Decoder-on-CLaMP 3 baseline; **kern vs interleaved ABC round-trip fidelity on PDMX; transcribe my own piano recording through the two-stage path as the first case-study fixture.

entries.title: Audio to score and a test of symbolic control
entries.summary: Promote direct audio-to-score research into the core reading path, correct its treatment in the report, and evaluate explicit melody control with YuE2 after unsuccessful ACE-Step listening tests.
entries.stage: Audio-to-Score paper reviewed; reference list corrected; four YuE2 pilot candidates and one cap-extension rerender complete. Musical quality awaits listening.
entries.focus: Measure transcription, notation conversion, and audible score adherence separately.
entries.next_step: Listen to all YuE2 candidates against the melody guide, then evaluate direct lead-sheet transcription against reviewed notation.

entries.title: YuE2 experiments in musical control
entries.summary: YuE2 produced an acceptable original song from lyrics and style, but score-conditioned arrangements and vocal layering were less convincing in my listening.
entries.stage: YuE2 inference trials complete; informal listening favors the original song. No model training or controlled cross-model ranking.
entries.focus: Find where score-conditioned generation fails: score reading, format conversion, or audible melody following.
entries.next_step: Plan a staged YuE2 imitation test: validate PDF/image-to-MusicXML, check MusicXML/MIDI-to-ABC conversion, then compare simple melody generation from verified notation and solo-piano audio. Not yet run.

entries.title: Where the score gets lost
entries.summary: YuE2's score input is a lead sheet: a third of the printed notes can be sent at all, OMR reads the melody but no chord symbols, the melody that is sent comes back loosely (80% recall alone, worse with chord symbols), and Stable Audio Open keeps the recording's harmony but not its register.
entries.stage: Score reading, interface capacity and melody following measured on one arrangement; Stable Audio Open text and audio-to-audio trials rendered and measured. No training.
entries.focus: Locate where a printed arrangement is lost on its way into a generator, and measure adherence instead of describing it.
entries.next_step: Listen to the 014 and 015 clips and the OMR renderings, compare the Stable Audio orchestra clips with the October 5 LEGO attempt, test the audio-first SheetSage2 path, and rerun the full 87 bars melody-only.

entries.title: What the reader keeps and what the singer keeps
entries.summary: On clean engravings open OMR reads both hands and the chord tones completely (homr 100% of K. 545, also from a phone photograph), so the 79–86% on commercial sheets is a layout and typography gap; YuE2 sings She in register but keeps 37% of the line against a 71% ceiling; MusicGen-melody, with no notation input, follows the same lines better (96% of She in order, an 18-note run), and EnCodec loses none of the harmony.
entries.stage: OMR graded against exact ground truth in three page conditions; She read, transcribed, sung by YuE2 and measured; MusicGen-melody and EnCodec round trips rendered and measured. No training.
entries.focus: Separate the page reader from the melody follower, and measure each against a known answer.
entries.next_step: Extend the benchmark toward real pages one feature at a time (lyrics, vocal-plus-piano systems, chord symbols, older fonts, repeats); longer MusicGen windows by continuation; YuE2 on the She line with cot=melody and no chord symbols; listen to the 016 and 018 clips.

entries.title: Music Transformer, reproduced and running in the browser
entries.summary: The released Music Transformer configuration, re-implemented in PyTorch and trained for one million steps on the official MAESTRO v1 split, reaches validation NLL 1.835 on the selection metric (the paper reports 1.835), 1.827 on every validation event and 1.801 on test; the port matches the original Tensor2Tensor code to float32 rounding, and the trained model now runs in the browser at 29 ms per event with a pianist-or-model blind test.
entries.stage: Music Transformer reproduced and checked: 16.1M parameters, 1,000,000 steps, 9.1 GPU-hours; validation NLL 1.835 (128 windows), 1.827 (full), test 1.801. Attention ablations training. The model runs in the browser.
entries.focus: Turn the reproduced model into the measuring instrument: the same held-out events for every extension, and ears only after the numbers.
entries.next_step: Finish the attention ablations; evaluate whole performances and longer contexts without retraining; adapt the model to one composer at a two-minute budget and measure on that composer's held-out pieces.

entries.title: Four score readers on one ruler: the notes and the structure live in different engines
entries.summary: Four released score readers on the same pages and graders: homr reads the most notes on every set (100% on rendered truth, 91.7% of right-hand notes on 200 real IMSLP scans) but has the worst tree-edit score (0.475); Zeus, a 2024 model trained on renders of the same Lieder corpus, scores 0.144 with fewer notes right; the 2026 full-page models Transcoda and LEGATO are third and fourth on every set, with runaway decoding on dense commercial pages.
entries.stage: OMR standings on a shared ruler: note recall and tree edit distance measured for homr, Zeus, Transcoda and LEGATO on rendered truth, 200 real scans with exact truth, and commercial pages. homr for notes, Zeus for structure, no engine for both; LEGATO's row on the real scans pending.
entries.focus: A reader that scores on both rulers at once on the same 200 scanned systems: note recall at or above 92% and TEDn at or below 0.14.
entries.next_step: LEGATO on the 200 OLiMPiC systems; an engraving post-pass on homr's output to measure how much of its tree-edit gap is derivable; then a reader trained on renders of the target corpus with a decoder that cannot run away.
